    "output": "<path>/source/head/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: #!/bin/sh\n2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n4: #\n5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the\n7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces\n8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n11: # startup config.\n12: #\n13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and\n19: #      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n27: #      path in its own routing table (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n31: #\n32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is\n36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are\n37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu\n38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and\n39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n41: #\n42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n47: #   official image's own variables:\n48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n52: #   address on the management network.\n53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n56: #   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n57: #   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)\n59: #   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n60: #   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt table step failed\n61: #\n62: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n63: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n64: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n65: \n66: set -u\n67: \n68: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n69: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\n70: USERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\n71: PASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\n72: HOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\n73: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n74:     case \"$1\" in\n75:         --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n76:         --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n77:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n78:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n79:         --trace) shift ;;\n80:         *) shift ;;\n81:     esac\n82: done\n83: [ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n84: \n85: CPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\n86: DISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\n87: INTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\n88: BOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\n89: INTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\n90: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n91: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n92: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\n93: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\n94: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\n95: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\n96: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\n97: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n98: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n99: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\n100: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\n101: MGMT_BR=br0\n102: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n103: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\n104: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\n105: SYSNET=/sys/class/net\n106: \n107: log() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\n108: rm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n109: \n110: FETCH_PORT=8080\n111: \n112: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\n113: IMG=\"\"\n114: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\n115: if [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n116:     log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n117:     exit 1\n118: fi\n119: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\n120: disk_bytes() {\n121:     case \"$1\" in\n122:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n123:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n124:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n125:         *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n126:     esac\n127: }\n128: want_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\n129: cur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\n130: if [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; then\n131:     truncate -s \"$DISK\" \"$IMG\"\n132: fi\n133: \n134: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------\n135: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here\n136: count_intfs() { ls -d \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }\n137: waited=0\n138: while [ \"$(count_intfs)\" -lt \"$INTFS\" ] && [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$INTF_WAIT\" ]; do\n139:     sleep 1\n140:     waited=$((waited + 1))\n141: done\n142: log \"interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s\"\n143: \n144: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------\n145: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.\n146: case \"$(uname -m)\" in\n147:     aarch64|arm64)\n148:         QEMU=\"qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd\"\n149:         PCI_BRIDGES=0\n150:         TCG_CPU=\"-cpu cortex-a57\" ;;\n151:     *)\n152:         QEMU=\"qemu-system-x86_64\"\n153:         PCI_BRIDGES=1\n154:         TCG_CPU=\"\" ;;\n155: esac\n156: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then\n157:     ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\n158: else\n159:     ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n160:     log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\n161: fi\n162: \n163: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n164: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n165: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n166: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n167: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\n168: node_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n169: case \"$node_id\" in\n170:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n171:     *)\n172:         e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n173:         if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n174:             o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n175:             node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n176:         else\n177:             node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n178:         fi\n179:         printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n180:             || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n181:         ;;\n182: esac\n183: NET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\n184: \n185: check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices the NIC layout cannot hold\n186:     # The last MAC octet holds the NIC index; zero belongs to management.\n187:     if [ \"$1\" -gt 255 ]; then\n188:         log \"at most 255 data NICs are supported (eth255 / ether256); index $1 would reuse a NIC MAC\"\n189:         return 1\n190:     fi\n191:     # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.\n192:     if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" != 1 ] && [ \"$1\" -gt 29 ]; then\n193:         log \"at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk\"\n194:         return 1\n195:     fi\n196: }\n197: \n198: qemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments\n199:     case \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" in\n200:         1)\n201:             # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.\n202:             # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.\n203:             # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.\n204:             _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))\n205:             _slot=$(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))\n206:             if [ \"$_slot\" -eq 1 ]; then\n207:                 printf '%s ' \"-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0\"\n208:             fi\n209:             # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.\n210:             # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one\n211:             # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.\n212:             # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.\n213:             printf '%s' \"-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$_bridge,addr=$(printf '0x%x' \"$_slot\"),romfile=,vectors=2\"\n214:             ;;\n215:         *)\n216:             # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.\n217:             printf '%s' \"-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$1,mac=$2\"\n218:             ;;\n219:     esac\n220: }\n221: \n222: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----\n223: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix\n224:     ip -\"$1\" addr show dev \"$2\" 2>/dev/null \\\n225:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\\{0,1\\} \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n226: }\n227: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway\n228:     ip -\"$1\" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n229: }\n230: M4=\"$(ip_global 4 eth0)\"; M6=\"$(ip_global 6 eth0)\"\n231: G4=\"$(ip_gw 4)\"; G6=\"$(ip_gw 6)\"\n232: if [ -n \"$M4$M6\" ]; then\n233:     printf 'M4=%s\\nM6=%s\\nG4=%s\\nG6=%s\\n' \"$M4\" \"$M6\" \"$G4\" \"$G6\" > \"$MGMT_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n234: elif [ -f \"$MGMT_FILE\" ]; then\n235:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments\n236:     . \"$MGMT_FILE\"\n237: fi\n238: log \"management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}\"\n239: \n240: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap\n241: if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR\" ]; then\n242:     _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n243:     ip addr flush dev eth0\n244:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the\n245:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.\n246:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null\n247:     brctl addbr \"$MGMT_BR\"\n248:     brctl setfd \"$MGMT_BR\" 0 2>/dev/null\n249:     echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n250:     ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" address \"52:54:01:$node_id:00\"\n251:     ip link set tap0 mtu \"$_mtu\"\n252:     ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n253:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until\n254:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's\n255:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.\n256:     brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" tap0\n257:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \\\n258:         \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0\" \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0\" \\\n259:         \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0\" 2>/dev/null\n260: fi\n261: ip link set tap0 up\n262: ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" up\n263: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it\n264: VM_LL=\"fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00\"\n265: VM_EP=\"$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR\"\n266: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read\n267: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n268: # the address stays tentative.\n269: LL=\"\"\n270: bridge_ll() {\n271:     _w=0\n272:     while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n273:         LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n274:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n275:         [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n276:     done\n277:     [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n278: }\n279: \n280: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk\n281: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS\n282: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count\n283: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n284: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n285: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n286: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\n287: max=0\n288: for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n289:     [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n290:     n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n291:     [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\n292: done\n293: prev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n294: case \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n295: [ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n296: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n297: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n298: # the watcher bridges the late veths.\n299: case \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n300: [ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\n301: check_nic_index \"$max\" || exit 1\n302: [ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n303: \n304: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n305: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n306: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\n307: if [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n308:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\n309: fi\n310: \n311: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n312:     _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n313:     if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n314:         brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n315:         ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n316:         ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n317:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n318:         echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n319:         brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n320:     fi\n321:     brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n322:     ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n323:     ip link set \"br$1\" up\n324: }\n325: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n326: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n327: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n328: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\n329: watch_links() {\n330:     _warned=\"\"\n331:     while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n332:         i=1\n333:         while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n334:             if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n335:                 bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n336:             fi\n337:             i=$((i + 1))\n338:         done\n339:         for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n340:             [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n341:             n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n342:             [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n343:             case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n344:             _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n345:             log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n346:         done\n347:         sleep 2\n348:     done\n349: }\n350: \n351: i=1\n352: while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n353:     tap=\"tap$i\"\n354:     tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n355:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n356:     ip link set \"$tap\" up\n357:     mac=\"$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$i\")\"\n358:     NET=\"$NET $(qemu_data_nic \"$i\" \"$mac\")\"\n359:     i=$((i + 1))\n360: done\n361: \n362: # shellcheck disable=SC2086\n363: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n364:     -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n365:     -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n366:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n367:     $NET &\n368: QEMU_PID=$!\n369: trap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\n370: log \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\n371: watch_links &\n372: \n373: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\n374: json_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\n375: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n376:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n377:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n378:     # read timeout (default 20s).\n379:     _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n380:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n381:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n382:             --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n383:     else\n384:         wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n385:     fi\n386: }\n387: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n388: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n389: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw\n390: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,\n391: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite\n392: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed\n393: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.\n394: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived\n395:     _cl=\"$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')\"\n396:     [ -n \"$_cl\" ] || return 1\n397:     grep -q -m1 '^\\r*$' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null || return 1\n398:     [ \"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$1\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" -ge \"$_cl\" ]\n399: }\n400: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> \"<status> <body>\"\n401:     _f=\"/tmp/chr-rest.$$\"; rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"; mkfifo \"$_f\" || return 1\n402:     timeout \"$(( $4 + 5 ))\" nc \"$VM_EP\" 80 <\"$_f\" >\"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null &\n403:     _pid=$!\n404:     exec 7>\"$_f\"\n405:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: [%s]\\r\\nAuthorization: Basic %s\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n%s' \\\n406:         \"$2\" \"$VM_LL\" \"$(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\" \\\n407:         \"$(printf '%s' \"$3\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" \"$3\" >&7\n408:     _left=$4\n409:     while kill -0 \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete \"$_f.out\" && [ \"$_left\" -gt 0 ]; do\n410:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))\n411:     done\n412:     exec 7>&-\n413:     wait \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null\n414:     _st=\"$(head -n1 \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)\"\n415:     _body=\"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r')\"\n416:     rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"\n417:     printf '%s %s' \"${_st:-000}\" \"$_body\"\n418: }\n419: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a\n420: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently\n421: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.\n422: is_err() { case \"$1\" in *'\"error\"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }\n423: \n424: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------\n425: waited=0\n426: AUTH=\"\"\n427: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank\n428: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username\n429: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that\n430: # answers is the requested user.\n431: while [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n432:     for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n433:         rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n434:     done\n435:     [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n436:     if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n437:         log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n438:         exit 1\n439:     fi\n440:     sleep 2\n441:     waited=$((waited + 2))\n442:     if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n443:         log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n444:         wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n445:         exit 1\n446:     fi\n447: done\n448: log \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n449: \n450: # Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST\n451: # answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the\n452: # configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.\n453: # A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is\n454: # logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).\n455: ssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc \"$VM_EP\" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }\n456: ready() {\n457:     case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/service?name=ssh\")\" in\n458:         *'\"disabled\":\"false\"'*)\n459:             _t0=$(date +%s)\n460:             until [ \"$(ssh_banner)\" = \"SSH-2.0\" ]; do\n461:                 if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n462:                     log \"SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)\"\n463:                     break\n464:                 fi\n465:                 sleep 2\n466:             done\n467:             ;;\n468:     esac\n469:     touch \"$READY_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n470:     log \"RouterOS ready\"\n471: }\n472: \n473: # A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can\n474: # still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).\n475: bootstrap_fail() {\n476:     log \"credential bootstrap FAILED: $1\"\n477:     wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n478:     exit 0\n479: }\n480: \n481: # ---- management: ether1 addressing and its own routing table ----------------\n482: # ether1 gets the container's management addresses, and their return path lives\n483: # in a `mgmt` routing table selected by a rule on those source addresses: a\n484: # default route the lab adds to `main` (a static 0.0.0.0/0, a PPPoE client's\n485: # default route, a dual-WAN pair) would otherwise take SSH/REST replies away\n486: # from the management network while the data plane works. CHR's default ether1\n487: # DHCP client is disabled: the address is static. Everything is tagged\n488: # clab-mgmt and re-applied on every boot from the container's CURRENT addressing\n489: # (a restart can bring a new IP), while the bootstrap channel itself\n490: # (link-local) never depends on it.\n491: mgmt_fail() {\n492:     log \"management setup FAILED: $1 (redeploy the node: containerlab deploy --reconfigure)\"\n493:     wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n494:     exit 0\n495: }\n496: rest_has() { # rest_has <path?query>: the GET answered a non-empty JSON array\n497:     case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\")\" in '['*'{'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac\n498: }\n499: rest_add() { # rest_add <what> <path> <json>: a 2xx with no error object, else mgmt_fail with the router's detail\n500:     _r=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" \"$2\" \"$3\" 20)\"\n501:     case \"$_r\" in\n502:         2??\\ *) is_err \"$_r\" && mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r#* }\" ;;\n503:         *) mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r:-no response}\" ;;\n504:     esac\n505: }\n506: rest_count() { # rest_count <path?query>: number of objects the GET answered\n507:     rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\" | tr '{' '\\n' | grep -c '\"\\.id\"'\n508: }\n509: rest_clear() { # rest_clear <menu>: remove its clab-mgmt objects\n510:     _ids=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" | tr '{' '\\n' \\\n511:         | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | paste -sd, -)\"\n512:     [ -z \"$_ids\" ] || rest_add \"remove old $1\" \"$1/remove\" \"{\\\".id\\\":\\\"$_ids\\\"}\"\n513: }\n514: # The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with\n515: # the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.\n516: mgmt_in_place() {\n517:     _want=0\n518:     if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n519:         rest_has \"ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n520:         rest_has \"routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE\" || return 1\n521:         [ -z \"$G4\" ] || rest_has \"ip/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=0.0.0.0/0&gateway=$G4\" || return 1\n522:         _want=$((_want + 1))\n523:     fi\n524:     if [ -n \"$M6\" ]; then\n525:         rest_has \"ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n526:         _want=$((_want + 1))\n527:     fi\n528:     [ \"$(rest_count \"ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")$(rest_count \"ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")\" \\\n529:         = \"$([ -n \"$M4\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n \"$M6\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)\" ] || return 1\n530:     rest_has \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none\" || return 1\n531:     [ \"$_want\" -gt 0 ]\n532: }\n533: mgmt_setup() {\n534:     if mgmt_in_place; then\n535:         log \"management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}\"\n536:         return 0\n537:     fi\n538:     for _m in routing/rule ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear \"$_m\"; done\n539:     rest_has \"routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE\" \\\n540:         || rest_add \"routing table $MGMT_TABLE\" routing/table/add \\\n541:             \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",\\\"fib\\\":\\\"yes\\\",\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"}\"\n542:     _c=\"\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"\"\n543:     if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n544:         _net4=\"$(ipcalc -n \"$M4\" | sed -n 's/^NETWORK=//p')/${M4#*/}\"\n545:         rest_add \"ether1 address $M4\" ip/address/add \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$M4\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",$_c}\"\n546:         rest_add \"route $_net4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n547:             \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"$_net4\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n548:         [ -z \"$G4\" ] || rest_add \"default via $G4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n549:             \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"0.0.0.0/0\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"$G4\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n550:         rest_add \"routing rule for ${M4%/*}\" routing/rule/add \\\n551:             \"{\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"${M4%/*}/32\\\",\\\"action\\\":\\\"lookup-only-in-table\\\",\\\"table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n552:     fi\n553:     if [ -n \"$M6\" ]; then\n554:         rest_add \"ether1 address $M6\" ipv6/address/add \\\n555:             \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$M6\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"advertise\\\":\\\"no\\\",$_c}\"\n556:         # RouterOS normalizes the host bits of dst-address (::3/64 -> ::/64)\n557:         rest_add \"IPv6 route $M6 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ipv6/route/add \\\n558:             \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"$M6\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n559:         [ -z \"$G6\" ] || rest_add \"IPv6 default via $G6 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ipv6/route/add \\\n560:             \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"::/0\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"$G6%ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n561:         rest_add \"routing rule for ${M6%/*}\" routing/rule/add \\\n562:             \"{\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"${M6%/*}/128\\\",\\\"action\\\":\\\"lookup-only-in-table\\\",\\\"table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n563:     fi\n564:     _id=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/dhcp-client?interface=ether1\" | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n565:     [ -z \"$_id\" ] || rest_add \"disable the ether1 DHCP client\" ip/dhcp-client/set \\\n566:         \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"$_id\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}\"\n567:     # RouterOS's default ND entry (interface=all, ra-lifetime=30m) sends router\n568:     # advertisements on ether1 too, and every host on the management network\n569:     # with accept_ra would install the router as its IPv6 default route. An\n570:     # ether1 entry with ra-lifetime=none keeps the RAs harmless and withdraws a\n571:     # route a host already learned (a disabled entry does not override \"all\").\n572:     # /ipv6/nd keeps no comment, so its entry is found by interface.\n573:     _nd=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1\" | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n574:     if [ -n \"$_nd\" ]; then\n575:         rest_add \"ether1 router advertisements off\" ipv6/nd/set \\\n576:             \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"$_nd\\\",\\\"ra-lifetime\\\":\\\"none\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"no\\\"}\"\n577:     else\n578:         rest_add \"ether1 router advertisements off\" ipv6/nd/add \\\n579:             \"{\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"ra-lifetime\\\":\\\"none\\\"}\"\n580:     fi\n581:     # Prove they took (a transport flake answers an empty body, which is not\n582:     # an error by the set-contract).\n583:     if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n584:         rest_has \"ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4\" || mgmt_fail \"$M4 not on ether1\"\n585:         rest_has \"routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE\" \\\n586:             || mgmt_fail \"routing rule for ${M4%/*} not applied\"\n587:     fi\n588:     log \"management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in routing table $MGMT_TABLE\"\n589: }\n590: # Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the\n591: # management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request\n592: # refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC\n593: # before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).\n594: mgmt_attach() {\n595:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0\" ] || brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" eth0\n596:     ip link set eth0 up\n597:     for _pair in \"$G4 ${M4%/*}\" \"$G6 ${M6%/*}\"; do\n598:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # split \"gateway source\"; an empty half skips the pair\n599:         set -- $_pair\n600:         [ $# -eq 2 ] || continue\n601:         _t0=$(date +%s)\n602:         until case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" ping \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$1\\\",\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"$2\\\",\\\"count\\\":\\\"2\\\"}\")\" in\n603:                 *'\"received\":\"'[1-9]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; do\n604:             if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then\n605:                 log \"gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)\"\n606:                 break\n607:             fi\n608:             sleep 1\n609:         done\n610:     done\n611: }\n612: \n613: # Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. On a\n614: # restart the CHR disk keeps its config and the marker (in the container rw\n615: # layer) survives, so the bootstrap (which could wait forever if the config\n616: # disabled `www` or changed the account, or reject duplicate `add` lines) is\n617: # skipped. A fresh deploy recreates the container and the disk, so the marker\n618: # and the config are both gone and the bootstrap runs.\n619: if [ -f \"$DONE_MARKER\" ]; then\n620:     log \"already bootstrapped (restart): skipping config\"\n621:     mgmt_setup\n622:     mgmt_attach\n623:     ready\n624:     wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n625:     exit 0\n626: fi\n627: \n628: # ---- credentials + identity -----------------------------------------------\n629: # Every credential-establishing call is CHECKED: the ready marker never\n630: # advertises credentials that do not work.\n631: FACTORY=\"admin:\"\n632: rest \"$FACTORY\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 || FACTORY=\"admin:$PASSWORD\"\n633: if [ \"$USERNAME\" = \"admin\" ]; then\n634:     if [ -n \"$PASSWORD\" ]; then\n635:         out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/set \\\n636:             \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\"}\")\"\n637:         is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set admin password: ${out:-no response}\"\n638:     fi\n639:     AUTH=\"admin:$PASSWORD\"\n640: else\n641:     out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/add \\\n642:         \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$USERNAME\")\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\",\\\"group\\\":\\\"full\\\"}\")\"\n643:     is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}\"\n644:     AUTH=\"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"\n645:     # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the\n646:     # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated\n647:     # full-access account.\n648:     out=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" user/set \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}\")\"\n649:     is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}\"\n650:     if rest \"admin:\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n651:         bootstrap_fail \"factory admin still authenticates after disable\"\n652:     fi\n653: fi\n654: rest \"$AUTH\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \\\n655:     || bootstrap_fail \"the requested credentials do not authenticate\"\n656: out=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity/set \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\")\\\"}\")\"\n657: is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set identity: ${out:-no response}\"\n658: got=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity)\"\n659: case \"$got\" in\n660:     *\"\\\"name\\\":\\\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\\\"\"*) : ;;\n661:     *) bootstrap_fail \"identity not applied: ${got:-no response}\" ;;\n662: esac\n663: \n664: mgmt_setup\n665: mgmt_attach\n666: \n667: # ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------\n668: if [ -s \"$STARTUP_CFG\" ]; then\n669:     bridge_ll\n670:     # one-shot HTTP server on the bridge's link-local address; the router\n671:     # fetches from it through ether1 (fetch takes a zoned link-local address\n672:     # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)\n673:     {\n674:         printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\\r\\nContent-Type: text/plain\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\n\\r\\n' \\\n675:             \"$(wc -c < \"$STARTUP_CFG\")\"\n676:         cat \"$STARTUP_CFG\"\n677:     } | timeout 90 nc -l -s \"$LL%$MGMT_BR\" -p \"$FETCH_PORT\" >/dev/null 2>&1 &\n678:     sleep 1\n679:     fetch=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" tool/fetch \\\n680:         \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$LL%ether1\\\",\\\"port\\\":\\\"$FETCH_PORT\\\",\\\"src-path\\\":\\\"/config.auto.rsc\\\",\\\"mode\\\":\\\"http\\\",\\\"dst-path\\\":\\\"config.auto.rsc\\\"}\")\"\n681:     case \"$fetch\" in\n682:         *'\"status\":\"finished\"'*)\n683:             # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets\n684:             # CHR_BOOT_WAIT seconds.\n685:             result=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" import '{\"file-name\":\"config.auto.rsc\"}' \"$BOOT_WAIT\")\"\n686:             case \"$result\" in\n687:                 *'\"ret\":\"true\"'*)\n688:                     log \"startup config imported\"\n689:                     ;;\n690:                 *)\n691:                     # RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first\n692:                     # error: the lines before it ARE applied.\n693:                     detail=\"$(printf '%s' \"$result\" | sed -n 's/.*\"detail\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p')\"\n694:                     log \"startup config import FAILED: ${detail:-${result:-no response}};         "text": "#!/bin/sh\n# chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n# Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n#\n# The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n# /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the\n# node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces\n# the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n# it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n# management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n# startup config.\n#\n# What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n# with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n#   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n#   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n#      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n#      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and\n#      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n#      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n#   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n#      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n#      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n#   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n#      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n#      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n#      path in its own routing table (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n#      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n#      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n#   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n#\n# Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n# ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n# device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n# binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is\n# recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are\n# persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu\n# carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and\n# their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n# step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n#\n# Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n#   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n# Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n#   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n# Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n#   official image's own variables:\n#   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n#   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n# Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n#   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n#   address on the management network.\n# Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n#   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n# Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n#   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n#   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n#                                      own reason, with the line number)\n#   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n#   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt table step failed\n#\n# Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\nset -u\n\n# Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n# limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\nUSERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\nPASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\nHOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n        --trace) shift ;;\n        *) shift ;;\n    esac\ndone\n[ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n\nCPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\nDISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\nINTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\nBOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\nINTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\nSTARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n# Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n# container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\nDONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\nREADY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\nID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\nNICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\nMGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n# every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n# boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\nMGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\nMGMT_BR=br0\n# eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n# namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\nMGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\nSYSNET=/sys/class/net\n\nlog() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\nrm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n\nFETCH_PORT=8080\n\n# ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\nIMG=\"\"\nfor f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\nif [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n    log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n# Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\ndisk_bytes() {\n    case \"$1\" in\n        *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n        *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n    esac\n}\nwant_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\ncur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\nif [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; then\n    truncate -s \"$DISK\" \"$IMG\"\nfi\n\n# ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------\n# shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here\ncount_intfs() { ls -d \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }\nwaited=0\nwhile [ \"$(count_intfs)\" -lt \"$INTFS\" ] && [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$INTF_WAIT\" ]; do\n    sleep 1\n    waited=$((waited + 1))\ndone\nlog \"interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s\"\n\n# ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------\n# The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.\ncase \"$(uname -m)\" in\n    aarch64|arm64)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd\"\n        PCI_BRIDGES=0\n        TCG_CPU=\"-cpu cortex-a57\" ;;\n    *)\n        QEMU=\"qemu-system-x86_64\"\n        PCI_BRIDGES=1\n        TCG_CPU=\"\" ;;\nesac\nif [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then\n    ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\nelse\n    ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n    log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\nfi\n\n# MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n# node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n# interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n# a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n# boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\nnode_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$node_id\" in\n    [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n    *)\n        e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n        if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n            o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n            node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n        else\n            node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n        fi\n        printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n            || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n        ;;\nesac\nNET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\n\ncheck_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices the NIC layout cannot hold\n    # The last MAC octet holds the NIC index; zero belongs to management.\n    if [ \"$1\" -gt 255 ]; then\n        log \"at most 255 data NICs are supported (eth255 / ether256); index $1 would reuse a NIC MAC\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.\n    if [ \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" != 1 ] && [ \"$1\" -gt 29 ]; then\n        log \"at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n}\n\nqemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments\n    case \"$PCI_BRIDGES\" in\n        1)\n            # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.\n            # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.\n            # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.\n            _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))\n            _slot=$(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))\n            if [ \"$_slot\" -eq 1 ]; then\n                printf '%s ' \"-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0\"\n            fi\n            # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.\n            # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one\n            # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.\n            # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.\n            printf '%s' \"-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$_bridge,addr=$(printf '0x%x' \"$_slot\"),romfile=,vectors=2\"\n            ;;\n        *)\n            # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.\n            printf '%s' \"-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$1,mac=$2\"\n            ;;\n    esac\n}\n\n# ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----\nip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix\n    ip -\"$1\" addr show dev \"$2\" 2>/dev/null \\\n        | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\\{0,1\\} \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway\n    ip -\"$1\" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n}\nM4=\"$(ip_global 4 eth0)\"; M6=\"$(ip_global 6 eth0)\"\nG4=\"$(ip_gw 4)\"; G6=\"$(ip_gw 6)\"\nif [ -n \"$M4$M6\" ]; then\n    printf 'M4=%s\\nM6=%s\\nG4=%s\\nG6=%s\\n' \"$M4\" \"$M6\" \"$G4\" \"$G6\" > \"$MGMT_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\nelif [ -f \"$MGMT_FILE\" ]; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments\n    . \"$MGMT_FILE\"\nfi\nlog \"management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}\"\n\ntunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap\nif [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR\" ]; then\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    ip addr flush dev eth0\n    # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the\n    # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null\n    brctl addbr \"$MGMT_BR\"\n    brctl setfd \"$MGMT_BR\" 0 2>/dev/null\n    echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" address \"52:54:01:$node_id:00\"\n    ip link set tap0 mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n    # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until\n    # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's\n    # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.\n    brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" tap0\n    sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0\" \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0\" \\\n        \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0\" 2>/dev/null\nfi\nip link set tap0 up\nip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" up\n# RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it\nVM_LL=\"fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00\"\nVM_EP=\"$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR\"\n# The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read\n# once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n# the address stays tentative.\nLL=\"\"\nbridge_ll() {\n    _w=0\n    while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n        LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n            | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n        [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n}\n\n# NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk\n# eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS\n# numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count\n# never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n# every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n# config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n# back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\nmax=0\nfor d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n    [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n    n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n    [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\ndone\nprev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n# The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n# every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n# the watcher bridges the late veths.\ncase \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\ncheck_nic_index \"$max\" || exit 1\n[ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n\n# RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n# requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n# link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\nif [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n    MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\nfi\n\nbridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n        brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n        ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n        echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n        brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n    fi\n    brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n    ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n    ip link set \"br$1\" up\n}\n# A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n# right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n# redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n# interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\nwatch_links() {\n    _warned=\"\"\n    while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        i=1\n        while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n            if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n                bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n            fi\n            i=$((i + 1))\n        done\n        for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n            [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n            n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n            [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n            case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n            _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n            log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n        done\n        sleep 2\n    done\n}\n\ni=1\nwhile [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n    tap=\"tap$i\"\n    tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n    [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n    ip link set \"$tap\" up\n    mac=\"$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$i\")\"\n    NET=\"$NET $(qemu_data_nic \"$i\" \"$mac\")\"\n    i=$((i + 1))\ndone\n\n# shellcheck disable=SC2086\n$QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n    -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n    -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n    -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n    $NET &\nQEMU_PID=$!\ntrap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; wait \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT\nlog \"qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)\"\nwatch_links &\n\n# ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------\njson_str() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | sed 's/\\\\/\\\\\\\\/g; s/\"/\\\\\"/g'; }\nrest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]\n    # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI\n    # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the\n    # read timeout (default 20s).\n    _auth=\"Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\"\n    if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n            --header \"$_auth\" --post-data \"$3\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    else\n        wget -q -O- -T \"${REST_T:-20}\" --header \"$_auth\" \"http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2\" 2>/dev/null\n    fi\n}\n# busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts\n# its diagnosis ONLY there ({\"detail\":\"Script Error: … (line N column M)\"}; its\n# /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw\n# HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,\n# reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite\n# `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed\n# once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.\nresp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived\n    _cl=\"$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')\"\n    [ -n \"$_cl\" ] || return 1\n    grep -q -m1 '^\\r*$' \"$1\" 2>/dev/null || return 1\n    [ \"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$1\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" -ge \"$_cl\" ]\n}\nrest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> \"<status> <body>\"\n    _f=\"/tmp/chr-rest.$$\"; rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"; mkfifo \"$_f\" || return 1\n    timeout \"$(( $4 + 5 ))\" nc \"$VM_EP\" 80 <\"$_f\" >\"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null &\n    _pid=$!\n    exec 7>\"$_f\"\n    printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: [%s]\\r\\nAuthorization: Basic %s\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n%s' \\\n        \"$2\" \"$VM_LL\" \"$(printf '%s' \"$1\" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\" \\\n        \"$(printf '%s' \"$3\" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')\" \"$3\" >&7\n    _left=$4\n    while kill -0 \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete \"$_f.out\" && [ \"$_left\" -gt 0 ]; do\n        sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))\n    done\n    exec 7>&-\n    wait \"$_pid\" 2>/dev/null\n    _st=\"$(head -n1 \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)\"\n    _body=\"$(sed '1,/^\\r*$/d' \"$_f.out\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r')\"\n    rm -f \"$_f\" \"$_f.out\"\n    printf '%s %s' \"${_st:-000}\" \"$_body\"\n}\n# RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a\n# bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently\n# failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.\nis_err() { case \"$1\" in *'\"error\"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }\n\n# ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------\nwaited=0\nAUTH=\"\"\n# A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank\n# password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username\n# asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that\n# answers is the requested user.\nwhile [ -z \"$AUTH\" ]; do\n    for _cred in \"admin:\" \"admin:$PASSWORD\" \"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"; do\n        rest \"$_cred\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH=\"$_cred\"; break; }\n    done\n    [ -n \"$AUTH\" ] && break\n    if ! kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        log \"qemu exited during boot\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    sleep 2\n    waited=$((waited + 2))\n    if [ \"$waited\" -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n        log \"RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running\"\n        wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\ndone\nlog \"RouterOS answered after ${waited}s\"\n\n# Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST\n# answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the\n# configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.\n# A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is\n# logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).\nssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc \"$VM_EP\" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }\nready() {\n    case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/service?name=ssh\")\" in\n        *'\"disabled\":\"false\"'*)\n            _t0=$(date +%s)\n            until [ \"$(ssh_banner)\" = \"SSH-2.0\" ]; do\n                if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge \"$BOOT_WAIT\" ]; then\n                    log \"SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)\"\n                    break\n                fi\n                sleep 2\n            done\n            ;;\n    esac\n    touch \"$READY_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    log \"RouterOS ready\"\n}\n\n# A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can\n# still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).\nbootstrap_fail() {\n    log \"credential bootstrap FAILED: $1\"\n    wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n    exit 0\n}\n\n# ---- management: ether1 addressing and its own routing table ----------------\n# ether1 gets the container's management addresses, and their return path lives\n# in a `mgmt` routing table selected by a rule on those source addresses: a\n# default route the lab adds to `main` (a static 0.0.0.0/0, a PPPoE client's\n# default route, a dual-WAN pair) would otherwise take SSH/REST replies away\n# from the management network while the data plane works. CHR's default ether1\n# DHCP client is disabled: the address is static. Everything is tagged\n# clab-mgmt and re-applied on every boot from the container's CURRENT addressing\n# (a restart can bring a new IP), while the bootstrap channel itself\n# (link-local) never depends on it.\nmgmt_fail() {\n    log \"management setup FAILED: $1 (redeploy the node: containerlab deploy --reconfigure)\"\n    wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n    exit 0\n}\nrest_has() { # rest_has <path?query>: the GET answered a non-empty JSON array\n    case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\")\" in '['*'{'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac\n}\nrest_add() { # rest_add <what> <path> <json>: a 2xx with no error object, else mgmt_fail with the router's detail\n    _r=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" \"$2\" \"$3\" 20)\"\n    case \"$_r\" in\n        2??\\ *) is_err \"$_r\" && mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r#* }\" ;;\n        *) mgmt_fail \"$1: ${_r:-no response}\" ;;\n    esac\n}\nrest_count() { # rest_count <path?query>: number of objects the GET answered\n    rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1\" | tr '{' '\\n' | grep -c '\"\\.id\"'\n}\nrest_clear() { # rest_clear <menu>: remove its clab-mgmt objects\n    _ids=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"$1?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" | tr '{' '\\n' \\\n        | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | paste -sd, -)\"\n    [ -z \"$_ids\" ] || rest_add \"remove old $1\" \"$1/remove\" \"{\\\".id\\\":\\\"$_ids\\\"}\"\n}\n# The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with\n# the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.\nmgmt_in_place() {\n    _want=0\n    if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n        rest_has \"ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n        rest_has \"routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE\" || return 1\n        [ -z \"$G4\" ] || rest_has \"ip/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=0.0.0.0/0&gateway=$G4\" || return 1\n        _want=$((_want + 1))\n    fi\n    if [ -n \"$M6\" ]; then\n        rest_has \"ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\" || return 1\n        _want=$((_want + 1))\n    fi\n    [ \"$(rest_count \"ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")$(rest_count \"ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT\")\" \\\n        = \"$([ -n \"$M4\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n \"$M6\" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)\" ] || return 1\n    rest_has \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none\" || return 1\n    [ \"$_want\" -gt 0 ]\n}\nmgmt_setup() {\n    if mgmt_in_place; then\n        log \"management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    for _m in routing/rule ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear \"$_m\"; done\n    rest_has \"routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE\" \\\n        || rest_add \"routing table $MGMT_TABLE\" routing/table/add \\\n            \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",\\\"fib\\\":\\\"yes\\\",\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"}\"\n    _c=\"\\\"comment\\\":\\\"$MGMT_COMMENT\\\"\"\n    if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n        _net4=\"$(ipcalc -n \"$M4\" | sed -n 's/^NETWORK=//p')/${M4#*/}\"\n        rest_add \"ether1 address $M4\" ip/address/add \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$M4\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",$_c}\"\n        rest_add \"route $_net4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n            \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"$_net4\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n        [ -z \"$G4\" ] || rest_add \"default via $G4 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ip/route/add \\\n            \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"0.0.0.0/0\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"$G4\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n        rest_add \"routing rule for ${M4%/*}\" routing/rule/add \\\n            \"{\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"${M4%/*}/32\\\",\\\"action\\\":\\\"lookup-only-in-table\\\",\\\"table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n    fi\n    if [ -n \"$M6\" ]; then\n        rest_add \"ether1 address $M6\" ipv6/address/add \\\n            \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$M6\\\",\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"advertise\\\":\\\"no\\\",$_c}\"\n        # RouterOS normalizes the host bits of dst-address (::3/64 -> ::/64)\n        rest_add \"IPv6 route $M6 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ipv6/route/add \\\n            \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"$M6\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n        [ -z \"$G6\" ] || rest_add \"IPv6 default via $G6 in table $MGMT_TABLE\" ipv6/route/add \\\n            \"{\\\"dst-address\\\":\\\"::/0\\\",\\\"gateway\\\":\\\"$G6%ether1\\\",\\\"routing-table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n        rest_add \"routing rule for ${M6%/*}\" routing/rule/add \\\n            \"{\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"${M6%/*}/128\\\",\\\"action\\\":\\\"lookup-only-in-table\\\",\\\"table\\\":\\\"$MGMT_TABLE\\\",$_c}\"\n    fi\n    _id=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ip/dhcp-client?interface=ether1\" | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n    [ -z \"$_id\" ] || rest_add \"disable the ether1 DHCP client\" ip/dhcp-client/set \\\n        \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"$_id\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}\"\n    # RouterOS's default ND entry (interface=all, ra-lifetime=30m) sends router\n    # advertisements on ether1 too, and every host on the management network\n    # with accept_ra would install the router as its IPv6 default route. An\n    # ether1 entry with ra-lifetime=none keeps the RAs harmless and withdraws a\n    # route a host already learned (a disabled entry does not override \"all\").\n    # /ipv6/nd keeps no comment, so its entry is found by interface.\n    _nd=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" \"ipv6/nd?interface=ether1\" | sed -n 's/.*\"\\.id\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n    if [ -n \"$_nd\" ]; then\n        rest_add \"ether1 router advertisements off\" ipv6/nd/set \\\n            \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"$_nd\\\",\\\"ra-lifetime\\\":\\\"none\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"no\\\"}\"\n    else\n        rest_add \"ether1 router advertisements off\" ipv6/nd/add \\\n            \"{\\\"interface\\\":\\\"ether1\\\",\\\"ra-lifetime\\\":\\\"none\\\"}\"\n    fi\n    # Prove they took (a transport flake answers an empty body, which is not\n    # an error by the set-contract).\n    if [ -n \"$M4\" ]; then\n        rest_has \"ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4\" || mgmt_fail \"$M4 not on ether1\"\n        rest_has \"routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE\" \\\n            || mgmt_fail \"routing rule for ${M4%/*} not applied\"\n    fi\n    log \"management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in routing table $MGMT_TABLE\"\n}\n# Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the\n# management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request\n# refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC\n# before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).\nmgmt_attach() {\n    [ -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0\" ] || brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" eth0\n    ip link set eth0 up\n    for _pair in \"$G4 ${M4%/*}\" \"$G6 ${M6%/*}\"; do\n        # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # split \"gateway source\"; an empty half skips the pair\n        set -- $_pair\n        [ $# -eq 2 ] || continue\n        _t0=$(date +%s)\n        until case \"$(rest \"$AUTH\" ping \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$1\\\",\\\"src-address\\\":\\\"$2\\\",\\\"count\\\":\\\"2\\\"}\")\" in\n                *'\"received\":\"'[1-9]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; do\n            if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then\n                log \"gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)\"\n                break\n            fi\n            sleep 1\n        done\n    done\n}\n\n# Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. On a\n# restart the CHR disk keeps its config and the marker (in the container rw\n# layer) survives, so the bootstrap (which could wait forever if the config\n# disabled `www` or changed the account, or reject duplicate `add` lines) is\n# skipped. A fresh deploy recreates the container and the disk, so the marker\n# and the config are both gone and the bootstrap runs.\nif [ -f \"$DONE_MARKER\" ]; then\n    log \"already bootstrapped (restart): skipping config\"\n    mgmt_setup\n    mgmt_attach\n    ready\n    wait \"$QEMU_PID\"\n    exit 0\nfi\n\n# ---- credentials + identity -----------------------------------------------\n# Every credential-establishing call is CHECKED: the ready marker never\n# advertises credentials that do not work.\nFACTORY=\"admin:\"\nrest \"$FACTORY\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 || FACTORY=\"admin:$PASSWORD\"\nif [ \"$USERNAME\" = \"admin\" ]; then\n    if [ -n \"$PASSWORD\" ]; then\n        out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/set \\\n            \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\"}\")\"\n        is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set admin password: ${out:-no response}\"\n    fi\n    AUTH=\"admin:$PASSWORD\"\nelse\n    out=\"$(rest \"$FACTORY\" user/add \\\n        \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$USERNAME\")\\\",\\\"password\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$PASSWORD\")\\\",\\\"group\\\":\\\"full\\\"}\")\"\n    is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}\"\n    AUTH=\"$USERNAME:$PASSWORD\"\n    # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the\n    # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated\n    # full-access account.\n    out=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" user/set \"{\\\"numbers\\\":\\\"admin\\\",\\\"disabled\\\":\\\"yes\\\"}\")\"\n    is_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}\"\n    if rest \"admin:\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        bootstrap_fail \"factory admin still authenticates after disable\"\n    fi\nfi\nrest \"$AUTH\" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \\\n    || bootstrap_fail \"the requested credentials do not authenticate\"\nout=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity/set \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"$(json_str \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\")\\\"}\")\"\nis_err \"$out\" && bootstrap_fail \"set identity: ${out:-no response}\"\ngot=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" system/identity)\"\ncase \"$got\" in\n    *\"\\\"name\\\":\\\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\\\"\"*) : ;;\n    *) bootstrap_fail \"identity not applied: ${got:-no response}\" ;;\nesac\n\nmgmt_setup\nmgmt_attach\n\n# ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------\nif [ -s \"$STARTUP_CFG\" ]; then\n    bridge_ll\n    # one-shot HTTP server on the bridge's link-local address; the router\n    # fetches from it through ether1 (fetch takes a zoned link-local address\n    # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)\n    {\n        printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\\r\\nContent-Type: text/plain\\r\\nContent-Length: %s\\r\\n\\r\\n' \\\n            \"$(wc -c < \"$STARTUP_CFG\")\"\n        cat \"$STARTUP_CFG\"\n    } | timeout 90 nc -l -s \"$LL%$MGMT_BR\" -p \"$FETCH_PORT\" >/dev/null 2>&1 &\n    sleep 1\n    fetch=\"$(rest \"$AUTH\" tool/fetch \\\n        \"{\\\"address\\\":\\\"$LL%ether1\\\",\\\"port\\\":\\\"$FETCH_PORT\\\",\\\"src-path\\\":\\\"/config.auto.rsc\\\",\\\"mode\\\":\\\"http\\\",\\\"dst-path\\\":\\\"config.auto.rsc\\\"}\")\"\n    case \"$fetch\" in\n        *'\"status\":\"finished\"'*)\n            # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets\n            # CHR_BOOT_WAIT seconds.\n            result=\"$(rest_raw \"$AUTH\" import '{\"file-name\":\"config.auto.rsc\"}' \"$BOOT_WAIT\")\"\n            case \"$result\" in\n                *'\"ret\":\"true\"'*)\n                    log \"startup config imported\"\n                    ;;\n                *)\n                    # RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first\n                    # error: the lines before it ARE applied.\n                    detail=\"$(printf '%s' \"$result\" | sed -n 's/.*\"detail\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p')\"\n                    log \"startup config import FAILED: ${detail:-${result:-no response}}; 5: // Package mikrotik_chr runs MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the official mikrotik/chr image.
6: //
7: // The image is MikroTik's own distribution (Alpine + qemu + the CHR disk) and is used
8: // unmodified: the kind writes chr-launch.sh into the node's lab directory, bind-mounts it
9: // read-only and sets it as the entrypoint in place of the image's /start.sh, which is not
10: // orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116, #3464).
11: package mikrotik_chr
12: 
13: import (
14: 	"context"
15: 	_ "embed"
16: 	"errors"
17: 	"fmt"

36: 	defaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials("admin", "admin")
37: 
38: 	InterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`ether(?P<port>\d+)`)

49: 
50: 	launcherFName = "chr-launch.sh"
51: 	launcherPath  = "/chr-launch.sh"
52: 	// readyFile is written by the launcher once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the
53: 	// startup config, and removed at every container start.
54: 	readyFile = "/.chr-launch-ready"
55: 
56: 	// mgmtComment tags every management object the launcher creates in RouterOS.
57: 	mgmtComment = "clab-mgmt"
58: 
59: 	// The last MAC octet is the NIC index; zero is reserved for management.
60: 	maxDataNICIndex = 255
61: 	// arm64's virt machine gets no PCI bridges: its single bus holds the disk, the
62: 	// management NIC and at most 29 data NICs before QEMU runs out of slots.
63: 	maxDataNICIndexARM64 = 29
64: 
65: 	// the launcher's CHR_INTF_WAIT and CHR_BOOT_WAIT defaults, and the time its config
66: 	// fetch and gateway check add, in seconds.
67: 	defaultIntfWait  = 60
68: 	defaultBootWait  = 300

74: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
75: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
76: 	platformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{
77: 		ScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs)
81: 
82: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
83: 		return new(mikrotikCHR)
84: 	}, nrea)
85: }

87: type mikrotikCHR struct {
88: 	clabnodes.VRNode
89: 	// goarch selects the NIC layout the interface limit is checked against. The
90: 	// containerlab binary's architecture matches the image's outside emulated setups.
91: 	goarch string
92: }
93: 
94: func (n *mikrotikCHR) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
95: 	n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)
96: 	n.ConfigDirName = configDirName
97: 	n.StartupCfgFName = startupCfgFName
98: 	// The image's qemu falls back to TCG emulation without /dev/kvm: KVM makes the boot
99: 	// fast but is not required.
100: 	n.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = false
101: 
102: 	n.Cfg = cfg
103: 	for _, o := range opts {
104: 		o(n)
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	// Credentials travel as env, not on the command line, so a password needs no quoting.
108: 	defEnv := map[string]string{
109: 		"USERNAME": n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
110: 		"PASSWORD": n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
111: 	}
112: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)
113: 
114: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,
115: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, configDirName), ":/ftpboot"),
116: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName), ":", launcherPath, ":ro"),
117: 	)
118: 
119: 	if n.Cfg.Entrypoint == "" {
120: 		n.Cfg.Entrypoint = "/bin/sh " + launcherPath
121: 	}
122: 	n.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf("--hostname %s", n.Cfg.ShortName)
123: 
124: 	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
125: 		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
126: 			Test:        []string{"CMD-SHELL", "test -f " + readyFile},
127: 			Interval:    5,
128: 			Timeout:     3,
129: 			Retries:     3,
130: 			StartPeriod: startPeriod(n.Cfg.Env),
131: 		}
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	n.InterfaceRegexp = InterfaceRegexp
135: 	n.InterfaceOffset = InterfaceOffset
136: 	n.InterfaceHelp = InterfaceHelp
137: 	n.goarch = runtime.GOARCH
138: 
139: 	return nil
140: }
