142: // dataNICLimit is the highest data NIC index the launcher's NIC layout holds on goarch.
143: func dataNICLimit(goarch string) int {
144: 	if goarch == "arm64" {
145: 		return maxDataNICIndexARM64
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	return maxDataNICIndex
149: }
150: 
151: // CheckInterfaceName rejects data NIC indices the launcher cannot create: beyond the
152: // free PCI slots on arm64, or wrapping the launcher's MAC addresses.
153: func (n *mikrotikCHR) CheckInterfaceName() error {
154: 	if err := n.VRNode.CheckInterfaceName(); err != nil {
155: 		return err
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	limit := dataNICLimit(n.goarch)
159: 	for _, ep := range n.Endpoints {
160: 		ifName := ep.GetIfaceName()
161: 		index, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(ifName, "eth"))
162: 		// An index too large for an int is still an index over the limit.
163: 		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrRange) {
164: 			return fmt.Errorf(
165: 				"node %q interface %q: cannot parse interface index: %w",
166: 				n.Cfg.ShortName, ifName, err,
167: 			)
168: 		}
169: 		if err != nil || index > limit {
170: 			return fmt.Errorf(
171: 				"node %q interface %q exceeds the maximum data NIC index %d on %s (eth%d / ether%d)",
172: 				n.Cfg.ShortName, ifName, limit, n.goarch, limit, limit+1,
173: 			)
174: 		}
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	return nil
178: }
179: 
180: // startPeriod is the healthcheck start period in seconds: the launcher's own worst case
181: // before the ready file, so a slow boot (TCG) never reports unhealthy. It waits up to
182: // CHR_INTF_WAIT for the links, then up to CHR_BOOT_WAIT each for REST, the startup-config
183: // import and the SSH banner, plus the config fetch and the gateway check.
184: func startPeriod(env map[string]string) int {
185: 	return envSeconds(env, "CHR_INTF_WAIT", defaultIntfWait) +
186: 		3*envSeconds(env, "CHR_BOOT_WAIT", defaultBootWait) + startPeriodSlack
187: }
188: 
189: // envSeconds reads a positive number of seconds from env, else returns def (the launcher
190: // falls back to its default the same way).
191: func envSeconds(env map[string]string, key string, def int) int {
192: 	if v, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(env[key])); err == nil && v > 0 {
193: 		return v
194: 	}
195: 
196: 	return def
197: }
198: 
199: // PreDeploy writes the launcher next to the startup config on every deploy, so a
200: // containerlab upgrade ships its launcher to existing labs.
201: func (n *mikrotikCHR) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
202: 	if err := n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params); err != nil {
203: 		return err
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	dst := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName)
207: 	if err := os.WriteFile(dst, launcherScript, clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {
208: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q: failed to write %s: %w", n.Cfg.ShortName, dst, err)
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	return nil
212: }

214: // PreStop skips VRNode's vrnetlab qcow2 alias step, which does not apply to this image.
215: func (*mikrotikCHR) PreStop(_ context.Context) error {
216: 	return nil
217: }

219: // SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS
220: // platform, see clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH) and writes it as the node's startup config,
221: // without the objects the launcher creates at every boot.
222: func (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(_ context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
223: 	exported, err := clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH(
224: 		net.JoinHostPort(n.Cfg.LongName, "22"),
225: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
226: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
227: 		"/export",
228: 	)
229: 	if err != nil {
230: 		return nil, err
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,
234: 		[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+"\n"))
235: }
236: 
237: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
238: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt routing table,
239: // its routes and rules), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1 DHCP client. Imported again
240: // as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the launcher already created and
241: // RouterOS stops the import at the first one; the management addressing also belongs to
242: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
243: // before
244: // matching.
245: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
246: 	var out []string
247: 
248: 	section := ""
249: 	pending := ""
250: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
251: 		if pending != "" {
252: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
253: 			pending = ""
254: 		}
255: 		if continues(line) {
256: 			pending = line
257: 			continue
258: 		}
259: 
260: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
261: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
262: 			section = trimmed
263: 		}
264: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
265: 			continue
266: 		}
267: 		out = append(out, line)
268: 	}
269: 	if pending != "" {
270: 		out = append(out, pending)
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
274: }
275: 
276: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
277: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
278: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
279: func continues(line string) bool {
280: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
281: 
282: 	return trailing%2 == 1
283: }
284: 
285: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
286: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
287: 		return false
288: 	}
289: 
290: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
291: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
292: 
293: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
294: 		return true
295: 	}
296: 
297: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
298: 	switch section {
299: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
300: 		return has("interface=ether1")
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	return false
304: }

err == nil && v > 0 {\n\t\treturn v\n\t}\n\n\treturn def\n}\n\n// PreDeploy writes the launcher next to the startup config on every deploy, so a\n// containerlab upgrade ships its launcher to existing labs.\nfunc (n *mikrotikCHR) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {\n\tif err := n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tdst := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName)\n\tif err := os.WriteFile(dst, launcherScript, clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q: failed to write %s: %w\", n.Cfg.ShortName, dst, err)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// PreStop skips VRNode's vrnetlab qcow2 alias step, which does not apply to this image.\nfunc (*mikrotikCHR) PreStop(_ context.Context) error {\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS\n// platform, see clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH) and writes it as the node's startup config,\n// without the objects the launcher creates at every boot.\nfunc (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(_ context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {\n\texported, err := clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH(\n\t\tnet.JoinHostPort(n.Cfg.LongName, \"22\"),\n\t\tn.Cfg.Credentials.Username,\n\t\tn.Cfg.Credentials.Password,\n\t\t\"/export\",\n\t)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\treturn clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,\n\t\t[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+\"\\n\"))\n}\n\n// filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:\n// every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt routing table,\n// its routes and rules), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1 DHCP client. Imported again\n// as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the launcher already created and\n// RouterOS stops the import at the first one; the management addressing also belongs to\n// the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined\n// before\n// matching.\nfunc filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {\n\tvar out []string\n\n\tsection := \"\"\n\tpending := \"\"\n\tfor line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, \"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\"), \"\\n\") {\n\t\tif pending != \"\" {\n\t\t\tline = pending + \"\\n\" + line\n\t\t\tpending = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tif continues(line) {\n\t\t\tpending = line\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttrimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)\n\t\tif strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, \"/\") {\n\t\t\tsection = trimmed\n\t\t}\n\t\tif launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout = append(out, line)\n\t}\n\tif pending != \"\" {\n\t\tout = append(out, pending)\n\t}\n\n\treturn strings.Join(out, \"\\n\")\n}\n\n// continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an\n// unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\\\`, so an even\n// run of trailing backslashes ends the line.\nfunc continues(line string) bool {\n\ttrailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\\`))\n\n\treturn trailing%2 == 1\n}\n\nfunc launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(line, \"add \") {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tfields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\\`, \" \"))\n\thas := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }\n\n\tif has(\"comment=\" + mgmtComment) {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\n\t// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.\n\tswitch section {\n\tcase \"/ip address\", \"/ipv6 address\", \"/ip dhcp-client\", \"/ipv6 nd\":\n\t\treturn has(\"interface=ether1\")\n\t}\n\n\treturn false\n}",

329: func TestFilterLauncherConfigEscapedBackslash(t *testing.T) {
330: 	// A value ending in a literal backslash is exported as `\\`: that line is complete and
331: 	// must not swallow the launcher line after it.

333: 		"add address=10.9.9.1/24 interface=ether2 network=10.9.9.0 comment=path\\\\\n" +

350: func TestContinues(t *testing.T) {
351: 	for line, want := range map[string]bool{
352: 		`add a=b`:     false,
353: 		`add a=b \`:   true,
354: 		`add a=b\\`:   false,
355: 		`add a=b\\ \`: true,
356: 		`add a=b\\\`:  true,
357: 		`add a=b\\\\`: false,
358: 	} {
359: 		if got := continues(line); got != want {
360: 			t.Errorf("continues(%q) = %v, want %v", line, got, want)
361: 		}
362: 	}
363: }

5: package mikrotik_chr

16: // launcherFunction isolates a shell function without running the disk, network,
17: // QEMU or REST operations at the top level of the embedded launcher.
18: // It assumes nested closing braces are indented; a nested brace at column zero
19: // would be mistaken for the end of the function.
20: func launcherFunction(t *testing.T, name string) string {
21: 	t.Helper()
22: 
23: 	_, body, ok := strings.Cut(string(launcherScript), "\n"+name+"() {")
24: 	if !ok {
25: 		t.Fatalf("launcher function %q not found", name)
26: 	}
27: 	body, _, ok = strings.Cut(body, "\n}\n")
28: 	if !ok {
29: 		t.Fatalf("launcher function %q has no closing brace", name)
30: 	}
31: 
32: 	return name + "() {" + body + "\n}\n"
33: }
34: 
35: func TestLauncherShellSyntax(t *testing.T) {
36: 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "/bin/sh", "-n")
37: 	cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(string(launcherScript))
38: 	if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
39: 		t.Fatalf("invalid launcher shell syntax: %v\n%s", err, out)
40: 	}
41: }

76: 	endpointName := e.GetIfaceName()

90: 			"Interface Mapping: Mapping interface %q (ifAlias) to %q (ifName)",
91: 			endpointName,
92: 			mappedName,
93: 		)
94: 		e.SetIfaceName(mappedName)
95: 		e.SetIfaceAlias(endpointName)

168: func preStopPrepareVrnetlabQcowAlias(ctx context.Context, d *DefaultNode) {
169: 	aliasName, ok := vrnetlabQcowAliasName(d.Config().Image)
170: 	if !ok {
171: 		log.Debugf(
172: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias skipped: unable to infer tag from image %q",
173: 			d.Config().ShortName,
174: 			d.Config().Image,
175: 		)
176: 		return
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
180: 	defer cancel()
181: 
182: 	// Some vrnetlab nodes rename the original versioned qcow image after first boot and fail on
183: 	// subsequent starts when they try to rediscover a versioned qcow filename. If there is exactly
184: 	// one non-overlay qcow file in / and our alias is absent, create a hardlink alias based on the
185: 	// image tag.
186: 	cmd := fmt.Sprintf(
187: 		`alias="/%s"; `+
188: 			`[ -e "$alias" ] && exit 0; `+
189: 			`src=""; `+
190: 			`if [ -f /sros.qcow2 ] && [ "/sros.qcow2" != "$alias" ]; then `+
191: 			`src="/sros.qcow2"; `+
192: 			`else `+
193: 			`set -- /*.qcow2; `+
194: 			`if [ "$1" != "/*.qcow2" ]; then `+
195: 			`for f in "$@"; do `+
196: 			`[ "$f" = "$alias" ] && continue; `+
197: 			`base="${f##*/}"; `+
198: 			`case "$base" in *overlay*.qcow2) continue ;; esac; `+
199: 			`if [ -n "$src" ]; then src=""; break; fi; `+
200: 			`src="$f"; `+
201: 			`done; `+
202: 			`fi; `+
203: 			`fi; `+
204: 			`[ -n "$src" ] || exit 0; `+
205: 			`ln "$src" "$alias"`,
206: 		aliasName,
207: 	)
208: 
209: 	execCmd := clabexec.NewExecCmdFromSlice([]string{"sh", "-lc", cmd})
210: 	res, err := d.RunExec(ctx, execCmd)
211: 	if err != nil {
212: 		log.Warnf(
213: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias preparation failed: %v",
214: 			d.Config().ShortName,
215: 			err,
216: 		)
217: 		return
218: 	}

134: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------
135: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here
136: count_intfs() { ls -d "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }
137: waited=0
138: while [ "$(count_intfs)" -lt "$INTFS" ] && [ "$waited" -lt "$INTF_WAIT" ]; do
139:     sleep 1
140:     waited=$((waited + 1))
141: done
142: log "interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s"
143: 
144: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------
145: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.
146: case "$(uname -m)" in
147:     aarch64|arm64)
148:         QEMU="qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd"
149:         TCG_CPU="-cpu cortex-a57" ;;
150:     *)
151:         QEMU="qemu-system-x86_64"
152:         TCG_CPU="" ;;
153: esac
154: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
155:     ACCEL="-cpu host -accel kvm"
156: else
157:     ACCEL="$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on"
158:     log "no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)"
159: fi
160: 
161: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per
162: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the
163: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on
164: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST
165: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).
166: node_id="$(cat "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
167: case "$node_id" in
168:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;
169:     *)
170:         e="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/address" 2>/dev/null)"
171:         if [ -n "$e" ]; then
172:             o2="${e##*:}"; rest_mac="${e%:*}"; o1="${rest_mac##*:}"
173:             node_id="$o1:$o2"
174:         else
175:             node_id="$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 "%02x:"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')"
176:         fi
177:         printf '%s\n' "$node_id" > "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
178:             || log "node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs"
179:         ;;
180: esac
181: NET="-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00"
182: 
183: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----
184: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix
185:     ip -"$1" addr show dev "$2" 2>/dev/null \
186:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\{0,1\} \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
187: }
188: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway
189:     ip -"$1" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
190: }
191: M4="$(ip_global 4 eth0)"; M6="$(ip_global 6 eth0)"
192: G4="$(ip_gw 4)"; G6="$(ip_gw 6)"
193: if [ -n "$M4$M6" ]; then
194:     printf 'M4=%s\nM6=%s\nG4=%s\nG6=%s\n' "$M4" "$M6" "$G4" "$G6" > "$MGMT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
195: elif [ -f "$MGMT_FILE" ]; then
196:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments
197:     . "$MGMT_FILE"
198: fi
199: log "management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}"
200: 
201: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap
202: if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR" ]; then
203:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
204:     ip addr flush dev eth0
205:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the
206:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.
207:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null
208:     brctl addbr "$MGMT_BR"
209:     brctl setfd "$MGMT_BR" 0 2>/dev/null
210:     echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
211:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" address "52:54:01:$node_id:00"
212:     ip link set tap0 mtu "$_mtu"
213:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" mtu "$_mtu"
214:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until
215:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's
216:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.
217:     brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" tap0
218:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \
219:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0" "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0" \
220:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0" 2>/dev/null
221: fi
222: ip link set tap0 up
223: ip link set "$MGMT_BR" up
224: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it
225: VM_LL="fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00"
226: VM_EP="$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR"
227: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read
228: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and
229: # the address stays tentative.
230: LL=""
231: bridge_ll() {
232:     _w=0
233:     while [ -z "$LL" ] && [ "$_w" -lt 20 ]; do
234:         LL="$(ip -6 addr show dev "$MGMT_BR" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \
235:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \(fe80::[^/]*\)\/64 .*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
236:         [ -n "$LL" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }
237:     done
238:     [ -n "$LL" ] || log "no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR"
239: }
240: 
241: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
242: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
243: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
244: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
245: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
246: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
247: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
248: max=0
249: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
250:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
251:     n="${d##*/eth}"
252:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
253: done
254: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
255: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
256: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
257: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
258: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
259: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
260: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
261: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
262: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
263: 
264: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
265: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
266: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
267: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
268:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
269: fi

1: // Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
2: // Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.

4: 
5: // Package mikrotik_chr runs MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the official mikrotik/chr image.
6: //
7: // The image is MikroTik's own distribution (Alpine + qemu + the CHR disk) and is used
8: // unmodified: the kind writes chr-launch.sh into the node's lab directory, bind-mounts it
9: // read-only and sets it as the entrypoint in place of the image's /start.sh, which is not
10: // orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116, #3464).
11: package mikrotik_chr
12: 
13: import (
14: 	"context"
15: 	_ "embed"
16: 	"fmt"
17: 	"net"
18: 	"os"
19: 	"path"
20: 	"path/filepath"
21: 	"regexp"
22: 	"slices"
23: 	"strconv"
24: 	"strings"
25: 
26: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
27: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
28: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
29: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
30: )
31: 
32: var (
33: 	kindNames          = []string{"mikrotik_chr"}
34: 	defaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials("admin", "admin")
35: 
36: 	InterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`ether(?P<port>\d+)`)
37: 	InterfaceOffset = 2
38: 	InterfaceHelp   = "etherX (where X >= 2) or ethX (where X >= 1)"
39: 
40: 	//go:embed chr-launch.sh
41: 	launcherScript []byte
42: )
43: 
44: const (
45: 	configDirName   = "ftpboot"
46: 	startupCfgFName = "config.auto.rsc"
47: 
48: 	launcherFName = "chr-launch.sh"
49: 	launcherPath  = "/chr-launch.sh"
50: 	// readyFile is written by the launcher once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the
51: 	// startup config, and removed at every container start.
52: 	readyFile = "/.chr-launch-ready"
53: 
54: 	// mgmtComment tags every management object the launcher creates in RouterOS.
55: 	mgmtComment = "clab-mgmt"
56: 
57: 	// the launcher's CHR_INTF_WAIT and CHR_BOOT_WAIT defaults, and the time its config
58: 	// fetch and gateway check add, in seconds.
59: 	defaultIntfWait  = 60
60: 	defaultBootWait  = 300
61: 	startPeriodSlack = 90
62: 
63: 	scrapliPlatformName = "mikrotik_routeros" //nolint: misspell
64: )
65: 
66: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
67: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
68: 	platformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{
69: 		ScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,
70: 	}
71: 
72: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs)
73: 
74: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
75: 		return new(mikrotikCHR)
76: 	}, nrea)
77: }
78: 
79: type mikrotikCHR struct {
80: 	clabnodes.VRNode
81: }
82: 
83: func (n *mikrotikCHR) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
84: 	n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)
85: 	n.ConfigDirName = configDirName
86: 	n.StartupCfgFName = startupCfgFName
87: 	// The image's qemu falls back to TCG emulation without /dev/kvm: KVM makes the boot
88: 	// fast but is not required.
89: 	n.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = false
90: 
91: 	n.Cfg = cfg
92: 	for _, o := range opts {
93: 		o(n)
94: 	}
95: 
96: 	// Credentials travel as env, not on the command line, so a password needs no quoting.
97: 	defEnv := map[string]string{
98: 		"USERNAME": n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
99: 		"PASSWORD": n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
100: 	}
101: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)
102: 
103: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,
104: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, configDirName), ":/ftpboot"),
105: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName), ":", launcherPath, ":ro"),
106: 	)
107: 
108: 	if n.Cfg.Entrypoint == "" {
109: 		n.Cfg.Entrypoint = "/bin/sh " + launcherPath
110: 	}
111: 	n.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf("--hostname %s", n.Cfg.ShortName)
112: 
113: 	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
114: 		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
115: 			Test:        []string{"CMD-SHELL", "test -f " + readyFile},
116: 			Interval:    5,
117: 			Timeout:     3,
118: 			Retries:     3,
119: 			StartPeriod: startPeriod(n.Cfg.Env),
120: 		}
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	n.InterfaceRegexp = InterfaceRegexp
124: 	n.InterfaceOffset = InterfaceOffset
125: 	n.InterfaceHelp = InterfaceHelp
126: 
127: 	return nil
128: }
129: 
130: // startPeriod is the healthcheck start period in seconds: the launcher's own worst case
131: // before the ready file, so a slow boot (TCG) never reports unhealthy. It waits up to
132: // CHR_INTF_WAIT for the links, then up to CHR_BOOT_WAIT each for REST, the startup-config
133: // import and the SSH banner, plus the config fetch and the gateway check.
134: func startPeriod(env map[string]string) int {
135: 	return envSeconds(env, "CHR_INTF_WAIT", defaultIntfWait) +
136: 		3*envSeconds(env, "CHR_BOOT_WAIT", defaultBootWait) + startPeriodSlack
137: }
138: 
139: // envSeconds reads a positive number of seconds from env, else returns def (the launcher
140: // falls back to its default the same way).
141: func envSeconds(env map[string]string, key string, def int) int {
142: 	if v, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(env[key])); err == nil && v > 0 {
143: 		return v
144: 	}
145: 
146: 	return def
147: }
148: 
149: // PreDeploy writes the launcher next to the startup config on every deploy, so a
150: // containerlab upgrade ships its launcher to existing labs.
151: func (n *mikrotikCHR) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
152: 	if err := n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params); err != nil {
153: 		return err
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	dst := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName)
157: 	if err := os.WriteFile(dst, launcherScript, clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {
158: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q: failed to write %s: %w", n.Cfg.ShortName, dst, err)
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	return nil
162: }
163: 
164: // PreStop skips VRNode's vrnetlab qcow2 alias step, which does not apply to this image.
165: func (*mikrotikCHR) PreStop(_ context.Context) error {
166: 	return nil
167: }
168: 
169: // SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS
170: // platform, see clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH) and writes it as the node's startup config,
171: // without the objects the launcher creates at every boot.
172: func (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(_ context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
173: 	exported, err := clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH(
174: 		net.JoinHostPort(n.Cfg.LongName, "22"),
175: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
176: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
177: 		"/export",
178: 	)
179: 	if err != nil {
180: 		return nil, err
181: 	}
182: 
183: 	return clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,
184: 		[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+"\n"))
185: }
186: 
187: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
188: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt routing table,
189: // its routes and rules), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1 DHCP client. Imported again
190: // as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the launcher already created and
191: // RouterOS stops the import at the first one; the management addressing also belongs to
192: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
193: // before
194: // matching.
195: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
196: 	var out []string
197: 
198: 	section := ""
199: 	pending := ""
200: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
201: 		if pending != "" {
202: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
203: 			pending = ""
204: 		}
205: 		if continues(line) {
206: 			pending = line
207: 			continue
208: 		}
209: 
210: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
211: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
212: 			section = trimmed
213: 		}
214: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
215: 			continue
216: 		}
217: 		out = append(out, line)
218: 	}
219: 	if pending != "" {
220: 		out = append(out, pending)
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
224: }
225: 
226: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
227: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
228: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
229: func continues(line string) bool {
230: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
231: 
232: 	return trailing%2 == 1
233: }
234: 
235: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
236: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
237: 		return false
238: 	}
239: 
240: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
241: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
242: 
243: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
244: 		return true
245: 	}
246: 
247: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
248: 	switch section {
249: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
250: 		return has("interface=ether1")
251: 	}
252: 
253: 	return false
254: }

Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined\n// before\n// matching.\nfunc filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {\n\tvar out []string\n\n\tsection := \"\"\n\tpending := \"\"\n\tfor line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, \"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\"), \"\\n\") {\n\t\tif pending != \"\" {\n\t\t\tline = pending + \"\\n\" + line\n\t\t\tpending = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tif continues(line) {\n\t\t\tpending = line\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttrimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)\n\t\tif strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, \"/\") {\n\t\t\tsection = trimmed\n\t\t}\n\t\tif launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout = append(out, line)\n\t}\n\tif pending != \"\" {\n\t\tout = append(out, pending)\n\t}\n\n\treturn strings.Join(out, \"\\n\")\n}\n\n// continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an\n// unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\\\`, so an even\n// run of trailing backslashes ends the line.\nfunc continues(line string) bool {\n\ttrailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\\`))\n\n\treturn trailing%2 == 1\n}\n\nfunc launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(line, \"add \") {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tfields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\\`, \" \"))\n\thas := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }\n\n\tif has(\"comment=\" + mgmtComment) {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\n\t// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.\n\tswitch section {\n\tcase \"/ip address\", \"/ipv6 address\", \"/ip dhcp-client\", \"/ipv6 nd\":\n\t\treturn has(\"interface=ether1\")\n\t}\n\n\treturn false\n}",

Now, the important detail on the MAC change:

Base: `mac="$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' "$node_id" "$((i & 255))")"` — masked to wrap.
Head: `mac="$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' "$node_id" "$i")"` — no mask, but check_nic_index limits to 255.

But: check_nic_index is called at line 301 with `$max`, and max could exceed 255 only if prev (NICS_FILE) or INTFS or existing ethN exceed. It exits 1 then. So no wrap.

Edge: what if node_id is "00:00"? MAC 52:54:00:00:00:ii — locally administered? 52:54:00 is QEMU's OUI, fine.

Another subtlety: the launcher check happens BEFORE writing NICS_FILE — good — but after bridges were... no, the NIC creation loop is after. Good.

Now, an important cross-check: the ARM64 limit. The comment says "one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs". QEMU virt machine: PCI slots 0..31? Actually on `virt` with default highmem, the PCI bus has 32 slots but some are reserved. The claim 29 data NICs max is consistent with comment. On amd64 default PC (i440fx), PCI bus has 32 slots (0-31), slot 0 reserved for the host bridge (pci.0 slot 0), IDE/ISA etc. take some slots. The old code created management NIC + data NICs up to ~28-29 max before QEMU ran out of slots. The PR adds bridges on amd64.

Now potential issue: on amd64, the data NICs are placed on bridges, but the management NIC stays on pci.0. The old limit of 29 on amd64 was that the mgmt NIC + ~28 data NICs. But wait: what about the virtio disk? `-drive file=...,format=raw` creates an IDE disk on the PC machine (not PCI). So the root bus holds mgmt NIC only (plus host bridge). And bridges each consume a slot on pci.0: bridge 1 at slot... auto-assign. So for 255 NICs → 11 bridges on pci.0, fine.

Now, one thing to verify: `-device pci-bridge` with `bus=pci.0` — on PC machine, pci.0 slots: the bridge device auto-assigns addr. Fine.

But hold on — an important detail: with `chassis_nr=$_bridge` — chassis_nr must be unique per bridge; ok.

Now the test expectation "old-limit" index 28: bridge 2, slot 3. (28-1)/25 = 1 → +1 = 2; (28-1)%25 = 27%25 = 2 → +1 = 3 → 0x3. Yes.

Wait, but the test case "old-limit" has `bridge: ""` — no bridge device emitted since slot != 1. But the bridge chrpci2 was emitted by index 26's call in the actual launcher loop. In the isolated test, the function output for index 28 alone references `bus=chrpci2` without emitting the bridge. That's fine for the isolated unit test but worth noting the test name is misleading? Not a defect.

Now check `TestQEMUDataNIC`'s "first-data-port": index 1 → bridge 1, slot 1 → emits `-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci1,chassis_nr=1,bus=pci.0 ` then netdev. Good.

Now check a real QEMU concern: `addr=$(printf '0x%x' "$_slot")` — slot 1..25 → 0x1..0x19. PCI bridge secondary bus: slots 0-31, but slot 0 is reserved for the bridge device itself on the bridge's own bus? On a PCI bridge's secondary bus, slot 0 is the bridge's downstream... actually slot 0 on a secondary bus is reserved (device 0 is where the bridge appears on the secondary bus). So slots 1..31 usable; 25 NICs is conservative. OK.

Now: does QEMU i440fx allow `-device pci-bridge` without an `addr` on pci.0? Yes, auto-assign.

Now the restart/renumber behavior: `check_nic_index "$max"` before persisting. Good.

Now potential issue #1: In `CheckInterfaceName` (Go), the arm64 limit of 29 is enforced based on `runtime.GOARCH` of the containerlab binary. Docs acknowledge this. Fine.

Potential issue #2: The Go check message for amd64 says "(eth255 / ether256)". But the actual launcher limit for the MAC is 255. Consistent.

Potential issue #3: `dataNICLimit` returns 255 for any non-arm64 goarch (e.g., "386", "ppc64le", riscv64). If containerlab binary is 386 (32-bit x86), the image is still amd64 presumably. Not a real concern.

Potential issue #4 — the launcher on amd64: `qemu_data_nic` uses `vectors=2`. virtio-net-pci vectors=2: one for RX/TX (single queue pair) + one config. Fine.

Potential issue #5 — `check_nic_index` only checks `$max`. But individual NIC creation loop goes 1..max; each NIC uses tap$i. The `ifname=tap$1` — tap names up to tap255. Fine.

Potential issue #6 — NICS_FILE persisting when check fails: check happens before NICS_FILE write. Good ordering.

Potential issue #7 — On amd64 with 255 NICs, MEM = 256 + 8*CPUS*255 ≈ 2.3 GB. Fine.

Potential issue #8 — the `qemu_data_nic` "append-only QEMU arguments" comment: the function output is used inside `$(...)` in a double-quoted string: `NET="$NET $(qemu_data_nic "$i" "$mac")"`. Command substitution strips trailing newlines; printf output has no newline. Word splitting: the output contains spaces but no quotes, so SC2086 splitting handles it. The `-device` and `-netdev` are one string with a space inside — after splitting becomes two words. OK.

But — one subtle bug: when `$_slot` computation overflows? No.

40: /// tab | Console
41: The serial console is on port 5000 inside the container:
42: ```bash
43: docker exec -it <node-name> nc 127.0.0.1 5000
44: ```
45: ///
46: /// tab | bash
47: ```bash
48: docker exec -it <node-name> sh
49: ```
50: ///
51: 
52: The node's management address is RouterOS's own `ether1` address ([transparent management](#management-connectivity)), so every service RouterOS runs answers on it directly, with nothing forwarded.
53: 
54: /// note
55: Default credentials are `admin:admin`. With custom [`credentials`](../nodes.md#credentials) the kind creates that user in the `full` group and disables the factory `admin` account, which has a blank password on a fresh CHR disk.
56: ///
57: 
58: ## Interface naming
59: 
60: You can use [interface names](../topo-def-file.md#interface-naming) in the topology file like they appear in RouterOS: `etherX`, where `X` is the port number.
61: 
62: * `ether2` - first data port
63: * `ether3` - second data port, and so on
64: 
65: /// admonition
66:     type: warning
67: Data ports start at `ether2`: `ether1` is the management interface. Using `ether1` in a topology results in an error.
68: ///
69: 
70: The container interface `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)`, also when links leave gaps: a link on `eth12` alone still lands on `ether13`, with `ether2` to `ether12` present and unlinked. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers.
71: 
72: On AMD64, data NICs are placed behind PCI bridges rather than sharing the default PC's root bus with all other devices. This removes the default layout's limit of 29 total Ethernet interfaces (management plus 28 data ports), so links can use `ether30` and higher without a custom launcher. ARM64 still uses a single PCI bus on the `virt` machine, shared with the disk and the management NIC; the PCI-bridge expansion applies only to AMD64.
73: 
74: /// admonition
75:     type: warning
76: The highest interface depends on the architecture, and larger indices are rejected during deployment:
77: 
78: * AMD64: `eth255` / `ether256`. The launcher's MAC-address scheme reserves index zero for management and uses one octet for the data-port index. This is an addressing limit, not a guarantee that every CHR version and host can run 256 interfaces.
79: * ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus.
80: 
81: The check uses the architecture of the containerlab binary, which matches the image's except in emulated setups.
82: ///
83: 
84: Sparse interface numbering also consumes VM resources for the intervening ports; memory defaults scale with the highest index, not just the number of links.
85: 
86: ## Node configuration
87: 
88: -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes boot with the default CHR configuration plus the credentials, the identity (set to the node name) and the management setup described below.
89: 
90: ### Startup configuration
91: 
92: A RouterOS script (`.rsc`) set with [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) is imported once the router is up:
93: 
94: ```yaml
95: name: chr_lab
96: topology:
97:   nodes:
98:     r1:
99:       kind: mikrotik_chr
100:       image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
101:       startup-config: r1.rsc
102: ```
103: 
104: The file is copied to the node's lab directory as `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` and imported over the REST API. RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first error: in that case the container log carries RouterOS's own reason with the line number, for example
105: 
106: ```
107: chr-launch: startup config import FAILED: Script Error: bad parameter network-type (line 3 column 59); lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not
108: ```
109: 
110: and the node does not become ready.
111: 
112: ### Saving configuration
113: 
114: [`containerlab save`](../../cmd/save.md) writes each node's `/export` to `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` in its lab directory. The management objects the launcher creates at every boot (everything tagged `clab-mgmt`, and the `ether1` DHCP client) are left out, so the saved file can be used as the startup config of the next deployment, also one with different management addresses.
115: 
116: ### Node readiness
117: 
118: The node is ready once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the startup config, reaches its gateway from the management address and, unless the configuration disables SSH, its SSH server answers. An SSH server that does not answer within `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` is logged, and the node is still declared ready, since REST and the console work. The container log then shows
119: 

(Showing lines 40-119 of 170. Use offset=120 to continue.)
</content>

Reasoning
The 02 test follows the 01 conventions. Good.

Now the 01-clab.yml for image reference; also, is `mikrotik/chr:7.24.5` the same image? Check 01-chr.clab.yml.

Also important: the 02 test uses `Require AMD64` — with `Skip If` in a Suite Setup. In Robot Framework, if Suite Setup fails, all tests fail; `Skip If` inside Suite Setup skips the suite (tests get skipped). OK.

But: the workflow matrix "02*.robot" will run on all runtimes; on ARM runners? The workflow runs on ubuntu-24.04 (x86_64). Fine.

Now, an important correctness check in the launcher: `check_nic_index` on amd64 with max > 29 but ≤ 255: bridges handle. But wait — the mgmt NIC and up to 11 bridges on pci.0: 11 bridge slots + mgmt slot = 12 slots out of ~29 free. OK.

But hold on — there's a deeper issue with the old-limit case on amd64: previously, amd64 had no bridges and max 28 data NICs. Now, data NIC 1..25 go on bridge 1... but the management NIC stays on pci.0. So existing behavior for ≤28 NICs changed: NICs now on bridge 1 instead of pci.0. Does RouterOS keep the same ether numbering? NIC order = PCI order = order of -device args. Comment says "NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below". With bridges, the PCI order is: bridges are devices on pci.0; data NICs on chrpci1 appear in the order they are created... QEMU assigns PCI devices in the order of creation for slot assignment. The -device args order: for index 1, we emit bridge1 then netdev d1; then d2..d25; then for 26: bridge2, d26... So the order of devices as seen by the guest: pci.0 devices in slot order — bridge1 gets an auto slot on pci.0, bridge2 gets the next... Actually QEMU auto-assigns addresses in command-line order. So bridge1 gets slot after mgmt NIC, bridge2 next, etc. And devices on bridges are in their own buses. The guest enumerates in PCI depth-first order: pci.0 devices in slot order: mgmt NIC (slot 2 presumably, slot 1 might be taken?), bridge1 (then its children), bridge2 (then its children)... So RouterOS sees mgmt first (ether1), then NICs on bridge1 in slot order (ether2..), then bridge2's NICs. That matches the index order. OK, the ordering holds.

But: MAC uniqueness within a node — the mgmt MAC last octet is 00, data NICs 01..ff. Fine.

Now — one more important check: the restart path. On restart, NICS_FILE has prev. If the lab changes (user removes the high port link), prev (e.g., 32) > current max → keeps 32 NICs. check_nic_index(32) passes on amd64. Fine.

Now what about the case where an existing container (deployed with the OLD launcher) had prev=40 on arm64 (allowed before? no — before, QEMU on arm64 virt would fail with >29ish NICs anyway; base had no check). If prev > 29 on arm64 with the new launcher, exit 1 → container fails to start. That's a behavior change for pre-existing labs on arm64 that somehow had >29 NICs — but those couldn't work before either (QEMU would have failed). OK.

Now, an important potential bug: `check_nic_index "$max" || exit 1`. The `$max` used includes `INTFS` which comes from CLAB_INTFS. If a user deploys with, e.g., 300 eth interfaces... Go check catches during deploy. But what about `containerlab deploy` with the container created before this check? CheckInterfaceName runs during deploy; endpoints are parsed. Good.

But wait — where is CheckInterfaceName called? default_node.go line 148: `err = d.OverwriteNode.CheckInterfaceName()` — in some function. Let me check which: probably in `CheckParameters` or similar, called at deploy. Let me confirm it's part of the deploy path. Line 148 in default_node.go. Let me read around.

289: watch_links() {

291:     while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do

293:         while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do

296:             fi

280: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
281: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
282: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
283: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
284: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
285: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
286: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
287: max=0
288: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
289:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
290:     n="${d##*/eth}"
291:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
292: done
293: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
294: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
295: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
296: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
297: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
298: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
299: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
300: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
301: check_nic_index "$max" || exit 1
302: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
303: 
304: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
305: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
306: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
307: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
308:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
309: fi

311: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)
312:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
313:     if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]; then
314:         brctl addbr "br$1"
315:         ip link set "br$1" mtu "$_mtu"
316:         ip link set "tap$1" mtu "$_mtu"
317:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge
318:         echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
319:         brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"
320:     fi
321:     brctl addif "br$1" "eth$1"
322:     ip link set "eth$1" up
323:     ip link set "br$1" up
324: }
325: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link
326: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's
327: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS
328: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.
329: watch_links() {

1: // Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs

4: 
5: // Package mikrotik_chr runs MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the official mikrotik/chr image.
6: //
7: // The image is MikroTik's own distribution (Alpine + qemu + the CHR disk) and is used
8: // unmodified: the kind writes chr-launch.sh into the node's lab directory, bind-mounts it
9: // read-only and sets it as the entrypoint in place of the image's /start.sh, which is not
10: // orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116, #3464).
11: package mikrotik_chr
12: 
13: import (
14: 	"context"
15: 	_ "embed"
16: 	"errors"
17: 	"fmt"
18: 	"net"
19: 	"os"
20: 	"path"
21: 	"path/filepath"
22: 	"regexp"
23: 	"runtime"
24: 	"slices"
25: 	"strconv"
26: 	"strings"
27: 
28: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
29: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
30: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
31: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
32: )
33: 
34: var (
35: 	kindNames          = []string{"mikrotik_chr"}
36: 	defaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials("admin", "admin")
37: 
38: 	InterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`ether(?P<port>\d+)`)
39: 	InterfaceOffset = 2
40: 	InterfaceHelp   = "etherX (where X >= 2) or ethX (where X >= 1)"
41: 
42: 	//go:embed chr-launch.sh
43: 	launcherScript []byte
44: )
45: 
46: const (
47: 	configDirName   = "ftpboot"
48: 	startupCfgFName = "config.auto.rsc"
49: 
50: 	launcherFName = "chr-launch.sh"
51: 	launcherPath  = "/chr-launch.sh"
52: 	// readyFile is written by the launcher once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the
53: 	// startup config, and removed at every container start.
54: 	readyFile = "/.chr-launch-ready"
55: 
56: 	// mgmtComment tags every management object the launcher creates in RouterOS.
57: 	mgmtComment = "clab-mgmt"
58: 
59: 	// The last MAC octet is the NIC index; zero is reserved for management.
60: 	maxDataNICIndex = 255
61: 	// arm64's virt machine gets no PCI bridges: its single bus holds the disk, the
62: 	// management NIC and at most 29 data NICs before QEMU runs out of slots.
63: 	maxDataNICIndexARM64 = 29
64: 
65: 	// the launcher's CHR_INTF_WAIT and CHR_BOOT_WAIT defaults, and the time its config
66: 	// fetch and gateway check add, in seconds.
67: 	defaultIntfWait  = 60
68: 	defaultBootWait  = 300
69: 	startPeriodSlack = 90
70: 
71: 	scrapliPlatformName = "mikrotik_routeros" //nolint: misspell
72: )
73: 
74: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
75: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
76: 	platformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{
77: 		ScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs)
81: 
82: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
83: 		return new(mikrotikCHR)
84: 	}, nrea)
85: }
86: 
87: type mikrotikCHR struct {
88: 	clabnodes.VRNode
89: 	// goarch selects the NIC layout the interface limit is checked against. The
90: 	// containerlab binary's architecture matches the image's outside emulated setups.
91: 	goarch string
92: }
93: 
94: func (n *mikrotikCHR) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
95: 	n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)
96: 	n.ConfigDirName = configDirName
97: 	n.StartupCfgFName = startupCfgFName
98: 	// The image's qemu falls back to TCG emulation without /dev/kvm: KVM makes the boot
99: 	// fast but is not required.
100: 	n.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = false
101: 
102: 	n.Cfg = cfg
103: 	for _, o := range opts {
104: 		o(n)
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	// Credentials travel as env, not on the command line, so a password needs no quoting.
108: 	defEnv := map[string]string{
109: 		"USERNAME": n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
110: 		"PASSWORD": n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
111: 	}
112: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)
113: 
114: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,
115: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, configDirName), ":/ftpboot"),
116: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName), ":", launcherPath, ":ro"),
117: 	)
118: 
119: 	if n.Cfg.Entrypoint == "" {
120: 		n.Cfg.Entrypoint = "/bin/sh " + launcherPath
121: 	}
122: 	n.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf("--hostname %s", n.Cfg.ShortName)
123: 
124: 	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
125: 		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
126: 			Test:        []string{"CMD-SHELL", "test -f " + readyFile},
127: 			Interval:    5,
128: 			Timeout:     3,
129: 			Retries:     3,
130: 			StartPeriod: startPeriod(n.Cfg.Env),
131: 		}
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	n.InterfaceRegexp = InterfaceRegexp
135: 	n.InterfaceOffset = InterfaceOffset
136: 	n.InterfaceHelp = InterfaceHelp
137: 	n.goarch = runtime.GOARCH
138: 
139: 	return nil
140: }
141: 
142: // dataNICLimit is the highest data NIC index the launcher's NIC layout holds on goarch.
143: func dataNICLimit(goarch string) int {
144: 	if goarch == "arm64" {
145: 		return maxDataNICIndexARM64
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	return maxDataNICIndex
149: }
150: 
151: // CheckInterfaceName rejects data NIC indices the launcher cannot create: beyond the
152: // free PCI slots on arm64, or wrapping the launcher's MAC addresses.
153: func (n *mikrotikCHR) CheckInterfaceName() error {
154: 	if err := n.VRNode.CheckInterfaceName(); err != nil {
155: 		return err
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	limit := dataNICLimit(n.goarch)
159: 	for _, ep := range n.Endpoints {
160: 		ifName := ep.GetIfaceName()
161: 		index, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(ifName, "eth"))
162: 		// An index too large for an int is still an index over the limit.
163: 		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrRange) {
164: 			return fmt.Errorf(
165: 				"node %q interface %q: cannot parse interface index: %w",
166: 				n.Cfg.ShortName, ifName, err,
167: 			)
168: 		}
169: 		if err != nil || index > limit {
170: 			return fmt.Errorf(
171: 				"node %q interface %q exceeds the maximum data NIC index %d on %s (eth%d / ether%d)",
172: 				n.Cfg.ShortName, ifName, limit, n.goarch, limit, limit+1,
173: 			)
174: 		}
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	return nil
178: }
179: 
180: // startPeriod is the healthcheck start period in seconds: the launcher's own worst case
181: // before the ready file, so a slow boot (TCG) never reports unhealthy. It waits up to
182: // CHR_INTF_WAIT for the links, then up to CHR_BOOT_WAIT each for REST, the startup-config
183: // import and the SSH banner, plus the config fetch and the gateway check.
184: func startPeriod(env map[string]string) int {
185: 	return envSeconds(env, "CHR_INTF_WAIT", defaultIntfWait) +
186: 		3*envSeconds(env, "CHR_BOOT_WAIT", defaultBootWait) + startPeriodSlack
187: }
188: 
189: // envSeconds reads a positive number of seconds from env, else returns def (the launcher
190: // falls back to its default the same way).
191: func envSeconds(env map[string]string, key string, def int) int {
192: 	if v, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(env[key])); err == nil && v > 0 {
193: 		return v
194: 	}
195: 
196: 	return def
197: }
198: 
199: // PreDeploy writes the launcher next to the startup config on every deploy, so a
200: // containerlab upgrade ships its launcher to existing labs.
201: func (n *mikrotikCHR) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
202: 	if err := n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params); err != nil {
203: 		return err
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	dst := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName)
207: 	if err := os.WriteFile(dst, launcherScript, clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {
208: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q: failed to write %s: %w", n.Cfg.ShortName, dst, err)
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	return nil
212: }
213: 
214: // PreStop skips VRNode's vrnetlab qcow2 alias step, which does not apply to this image.
215: func (*mikrotikCHR) PreStop(_ context.Context) error {
216: 	return nil
217: }
218: 
219: // SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS
220: // platform, see clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH) and writes it as the node's startup config,
221: // without the objects the launcher creates at every boot.
222: func (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(_ context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
223: 	exported, err := clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH(
224: 		net.JoinHostPort(n.Cfg.LongName, "22"),
225: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
226: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
227: 		"/export",
228: 	)
229: 	if err != nil {
230: 		return nil, err
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,
234: 		[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+"\n"))
235: }
236: 
237: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
238: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt routing table,
239: // its routes and rules), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1 DHCP client. Imported again
240: // as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the launcher already created and
241: // RouterOS stops the import at the first one; the management addressing also belongs to
242: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
243: // before
244: // matching.
245: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
246: 	var out []string
247: 
248: 	section := ""
249: 	pending := ""
250: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
251: 		if pending != "" {
252: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
253: 			pending = ""
254: 		}
255: 		if continues(line) {
256: 			pending = line
257: 			continue
258: 		}
259: 
260: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
261: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
262: 			section = trimmed
263: 		}
264: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
265: 			continue
266: 		}
267: 		out = append(out, line)
268: 	}
269: 	if pending != "" {
270: 		out = append(out, pending)
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
274: }
275: 
276: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
277: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
278: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
279: func continues(line string) bool {
280: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
281: 
282: 	return trailing%2 == 1
283: }
284: 
285: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
286: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
287: 		return false
288: 	}
289: 
290: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
291: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
292: 
293: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
294: 		return true
295: 	}
296: 
297: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
298: 	switch section {
299: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
300: 		return has("interface=ether1")
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	return false
304: }

1: #!/bin/sh
2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud
3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.
4: #
5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +
6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the
7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces
8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):
9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the
10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no
11: # startup config.
12: #
13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done
14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):
15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)
16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's
17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS
18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and
19: #      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only
20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred
21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,
22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container
23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps
24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is
25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,
26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return
27: #      path in its own routing table (`mgmt`, below), then fetches
28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)
29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it
30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu
31: #
32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an
33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW
34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never
35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is
36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are
37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu
38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and
39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management
40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.
41: #
42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,
43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.
44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]
45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env
46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the
47: #   official image's own variables:
48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),
49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)
50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container
51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no
52: #   address on the management network.
53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default
54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.
55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed "chr-launch:":
56: #   "RouterOS ready"                   login + startup config done
57: #   "startup config import FAILED: …"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's
58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)
59: #   "credential bootstrap FAILED: …"   the user/password step failed
60: #   "management setup FAILED: …"       the ether1 address / mgmt table step failed
61: #
62: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
63: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
64: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
65: 
66: set -u
67: 
68: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting
69: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.
70: USERNAME="${USERNAME:-admin}"
71: PASSWORD="${PASSWORD-admin}"
72: HOSTNAME_ARG=""
73: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
74:     case "$1" in
75:         --username) USERNAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76:         --password) PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
77:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
78:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;
79:         --trace) shift ;;
80:         *) shift ;;
81:     esac
82: done
83: [ -n "$HOSTNAME_ARG" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG="$(hostname)"
84: 
85: CPUS="${CPUS:-1}"
86: DISK="${DISK:-128M}"
87: INTF_WAIT="${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}"
88: BOOT_WAIT="${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}"
89: INTFS="${CLAB_INTFS:-0}"
90: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc
91: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the
92: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).
93: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped
94: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready
95: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id
96: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics
97: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt
98: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each
99: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out
100: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt
101: MGMT_BR=br0
102: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network
103: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare
104: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt
105: SYSNET=/sys/class/net
106: 
107: log() { echo "chr-launch: $*"; }
108: rm -f "$READY_FILE"
109: 
110: FETCH_PORT=8080
111: 
112: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------
113: IMG=""
114: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f "$f" ] && IMG="$f" && break; done
115: if [ -z "$IMG" ]; then
116:     log "no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image"
117:     exit 1
118: fi
119: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.
120: disk_bytes() {
121:     case "$1" in
122:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
123:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
124:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;
125:         *) echo "$1" ;;
126:     esac
127: }
128: want_bytes="$(disk_bytes "$DISK")"
129: cur_bytes="$(stat -c %s "$IMG" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$IMG")"
130: if [ "$cur_bytes" -lt "$want_bytes" ] 2>/dev/null; then

credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n# Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n#   official image's own variables:\n#   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n#   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n# Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n#   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n#   address on the management network.\n# Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n#   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n# Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n#   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n#   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n#                                      own reason, with the line number)\n#   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n#   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt table step failed\n#\n# Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\nset -u\n\n# Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n# limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\nUSERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\nPASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\nHOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n        --trace) shift ;;\n        *) shift ;;\n    esac\ndone\n[ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n\nCPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\nDISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\nINTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\nBOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\nINTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\nSTARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n# Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n# container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\nDONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\nREADY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\nID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\nNICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\nMGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n# every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n# boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\nMGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\nMGMT_BR=br0\n# eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n# namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\nMGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\nSYSNET=/sys/class/net\n\nlog() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\nrm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n\nFETCH_PORT=8080\n\n# ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\nIMG=\"\"\nfor f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\nif [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n    log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n# Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\ndisk_bytes() {\n    case \"$1\" in\n        *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n        *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n        *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n    esac\n}\nwant_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\ncur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\nif [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; 16: // launcherFunction isolates a shell function without running the disk, network,
17: // QEMU or REST operations at the top level of the embedded launcher.
18: // It assumes nested closing braces are indented; a nested brace at column zero
19: // would be mistaken for the end of the function.
20: func launcherFunction(t *testing.T, name string) string {
21: 	t.Helper()
22: 
23: 	_, body, ok := strings.Cut(string(launcherScript), "\n"+name+"() {")
24: 	if !ok {
25: 		t.Fatalf("launcher function %q not found", name)
26: 	}
27: 	body, _, ok = strings.Cut(body, "\n}\n")
28: 	if !ok {
29: 		t.Fatalf("launcher function %q has no closing brace", name)
30: 	}
31: 
32: 	return name + "() {" + body + "\n}\n"
33: }
34: 
35: func TestLauncherShellSyntax(t *testing.T) {
36: 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "/bin/sh", "-n")
37: 	cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(string(launcherScript))
38: 	if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
39: 		t.Fatalf("invalid launcher shell syntax: %v\n%s", err, out)
40: 	}
41: }

147: func TestInterfaceParsing(t *testing.T) {
148: 	tests := map[string]struct {
149: 		goarch  string // defaults to amd64, so the result doesn't depend on the test host
150: 		ifaces  []string
151: 		want    []string
152: 		wantErr bool
153: 		errText string // when set, the error must contain it
154: 	}{
155: 		"routeros-names": {
156: 			ifaces: []string{"ether2", "ether5", "ether13", "ether30", "ether33", "ether256"},
157: 			want:   []string{"eth1", "eth4", "eth12", "eth29", "eth32", "eth255"},
158: 		},
159: 		"eth-names": {
160: 			ifaces: []string{"eth1", "eth3", "eth255"},
161: 			want:   []string{"eth1", "eth3", "eth255"},
162: 		},
163: 		"mgmt-ether1":    {ifaces: []string{"ether1"}, wantErr: true},
164: 		"ether-overflow": {ifaces: []string{"ether257"}, wantErr: true, errText: "exceeds the maximum"},
165: 		"ether300":       {ifaces: []string{"ether300"}, wantErr: true, errText: "exceeds the maximum"},
166: 		"eth-overflow":   {ifaces: []string{"eth256"}, wantErr: true, errText: "exceeds the maximum"},
167: 		"eth300":         {ifaces: []string{"eth300"}, wantErr: true, errText: "exceeds the maximum"},
168: 		"integer-overflow": {
169: 			ifaces:  []string{"eth999999999999999999999999"},
170: 			wantErr: true,
171: 			errText: "exceeds the maximum",
172: 		},
173: 		// VMInterfaceRegexp is not anchored at the start, so this passes the parent check.
174: 		"malformed": {ifaces: []string{"xeth5"}, wantErr: true, errText: "cannot parse interface index"},
175: 		"duplicate": {ifaces: []string{"eth1", "eth1"}, wantErr: true},
176: 		"arm64-limit": {
177: 			goarch: "arm64",
178: 			ifaces: []string{"ether2", "ether30"},
179: 			want:   []string{"eth1", "eth29"},
180: 		},
181: 		"arm64-overflow": {
182: 			goarch:  "arm64",
183: 			ifaces:  []string{"ether31"},
184: 			wantErr: true,
185: 			errText: "exceeds the maximum data NIC index 29 on arm64 (eth29 / ether30)",
186: 		},
187: 	}
188: 
189: 	for name, tc := range tests {
190: 		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
191: 			n := newInitialized(t, &clabtypes.NodeConfig{ShortName: "r1", LabDir: t.TempDir()})
192: 			n.goarch = "amd64"
193: 			if tc.goarch != "" {
194: 				n.goarch = tc.goarch
195: 			}
196: 
197: 			var err error
198: 			for _, ifName := range tc.ifaces {
199: 				ep := &clablinks.EndpointVeth{
200: 					EndpointGeneric: clablinks.EndpointGeneric{IfaceName: ifName},
201: 				}
202: 				if err = n.AddEndpoint(ep); err != nil {
203: 					break
204: 				}
205: 			}
206: 			if err == nil {
207: 				err = n.CheckInterfaceName()
208: 			}
209: 
210: 			if tc.wantErr {
211: 				if err == nil {
212: 					t.Fatalf("interfaces %v: want an error, got none", tc.ifaces)
213: 				}
214: 				if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.errText) {
215: 					t.Errorf("interfaces %v: error %q, want it to contain %q", tc.ifaces, err, tc.errText)
216: 				}
217: 				return
218: 			}
219: 			if err != nil {
220: 				t.Fatalf("interfaces %v: %v", tc.ifaces, err)
221: 			}
222: 			for i, ep := range n.Endpoints {
223: 				if ep.GetIfaceName() != tc.want[i] {
224: 					t.Errorf(
225: 						"%q mapped to %q, want %q",
226: 						tc.ifaces[i],
227: 						ep.GetIfaceName(),
228: 						tc.want[i],
229: 					)
230: 				}
231: 			}
232: 		})
233: 	}
234: }

278: func TestFilterLauncherConfig(t *testing.T) {
279: 	got := filterLauncherConfig(exportedConfig)
280: 
281: 	if strings.Contains(got, "clab-mgmt") {
282: 		t.Errorf("filtered config still contains a clab-mgmt object:\n%s", got)
283: 	}
284: 	for _, gone := range []string{
285: 		"add disabled=yes interface=ether1 name=client1",
286: 		"add interface=ether1 ra-lifetime=none",
287: 		"172.20.20.4",
288: 		"3fff:172:20:20::4",
289: 	} {
290: 		if strings.Contains(got, gone) {
291: 			t.Errorf("filtered config still contains launcher line %q:\n%s", gone, got)
292: 		}
293: 	}
294: 
295: 	for _, kept := range []string{
296: 		"add address=10.0.0.2/30 interface=ether2 network=10.0.0.0",
297: 		"add address=2.2.2.2 interface=lo0 network=2.2.2.2",
298: 		"add dst-address=0.0.0.0/0 gateway=10.0.0.1",
299: 		"add name=lo0",
300: 		"set name=r2",
301: 		"/routing table",
302: 	} {

304: 			t.Errorf("filtered config lost user line %q:\n%s", kept, got)

306: 	}

329: func TestFilterLauncherConfigEscapedBackslash(t *testing.T) {
330: 	// A value ending in a literal backslash is exported as `\\`: that line is complete and
331: 	// must not swallow the launcher line after it.
332: 	in := "/ip address\n" +
333: 		"add address=10.9.9.1/24 interface=ether2 network=10.9.9.0 comment=path\\\\\n" +
334: 		"add address=172.20.20.3/24 comment=clab-mgmt interface=ether1 network=\\\n" +
335: 		"    172.20.20.0\n"
336: 
337: 	got := filterLauncherConfig(in)
338: 
339: 	if !strings.Contains(
340: 		got,
341: 		"add address=10.9.9.1/24 interface=ether2 network=10.9.9.0 comment=path",
342: 	) {
343: 		t.Errorf("user address ending in an escaped backslash was dropped:\n%s", got)
344: 	}
345: 	if strings.Contains(got, "clab-mgmt") {
346: 		t.Errorf("launcher address kept:\n%s", got)
347: 	}
348: }

350: func TestContinues(t *testing.T) {
351: 	for line, want := range map[string]bool{
352: 		`add a=b`:     false,
353: 		`add a=b \`:   true,
354: 		`add a=b\\`:   false,
355: 		`add a=b\\ \`: true,
356: 		`add a=b\\\`:  true,
357: 		`add a=b\\\\`: false,
358: 	} {
359: 		if got := continues(line); got != want {
360: 			t.Errorf("continues(%q) = %v, want %v", line, got, want)
361: 		}
362: 	}
363: }
